name: North Dakota

agency.name: North Dakota Department of Labor and Human Rights, Wage & Hour Division

rates2026.note: Unchanged throughout 2026; same as the federal minimum

tipped.note: Tip credit of 33% of the minimum wage; tipped employee = more than $30/month in tips; employer must ensure the full $7.25 with tips

minWage.other: Sub-minimum wages only under a Department license (Sub-minimum Wage Licensing).

source.quote: Effective Date: August 1, 2015 MINIMUM WAGE RATE: $7.25

overtime.note: Compensatory time is not legal for non-exempt private employees.

source.quote: Overtime pay must be paid at one and one-half times the employee's regular rate of pay for hours worked over forty in any work week.

sickLeave.note: No state paid sick leave law for private employers.

finalPay.fired: by the next regular payday for the period worked; sent by certified mail (or as agreed)
finalPay.quit: by the next regular payday for the period worked
finalPay.ptoNote: Paid time off made available for use is wages at separation and cannot be forfeited; exceptions: voluntary quit with under 1 year of service and less than 5 days' notice if the employee was told in writing at hire, and awarded-but-unearned PTO. Use-it-or-lose-it allowed with notice.

source.quote: unpaid wages or compensation become due and payable at the regular payday(s) established in advance by the employer for the period(s) worked by the employee.

ptoSource.quote: Once paid time off is made available for an employee's use, any unused portion of such time is considered wages upon separation from employment and must be paid

breaks.meal: 30-minute meal period for shifts over 5 hours when two or more employees are on duty (employee may waive)

source.quote: A minimum 30-minute meal period must be provided in shifts exceeding five hours when there are two or more employees on duty.

rightToWorkSource.quote: RIGHT TO WORK N.D.C.C. § 34-01-14 An individual's right to work may not be denied or abridged due to membership or nonmembership in any labor union

notes.text: Unlike most states, North Dakota treats accrued vacation/PTO as wages that must be paid out at separation; a policy cannot make it forfeit (narrow exceptions).

source.quote: No employment contract or policy may provide for forfeiture of earned paid time off upon separation.

notes.text: When an employer fires someone, the final paycheck must be sent by certified mail to an address the employee designates, unless agreed otherwise.

source.quote: When an employer terminates an employee, the employer shall pay those wages to the employee by certified mail at an address designated by the employee

uncertain: Rates and rules taken from the official ND Minimum Wage & Work Conditions Summary Poster (minimum wage effective 2015); the nd.gov FAQ page loads by script and could not be read. $7.25 cross-checked on dol.gov state table (updated 2026-07-01).
